newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends steady ahead of holidays.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends steady ahead of holidays.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES -Prices ended the day steady with small gains recorded but trading was thin ahead of the Chinese New year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr holidays. There was some book-squaring and unwinding of positions and late covering. April futures saw support at 1,300 level.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Market held steady on pre-holiday covering, with interest seen among selected oils. Market re-opens on February 12.
The market is closed from February 6 until 11 for both the festivals and re-opens on February 12.

Traders said a crop report by forecaster Ivan Wong had no impact on the market. "Ivan's figures were within market estimates and the market did not move aggressively at all," a trader said. Malaysia's palm oil output in January is estimated to have fallen by 9.5 percent to 578,000 tonnes from December 1996, Wong said on Wednesday.
Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of January at 725,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 792,687 tonnes at end-December.
Exports in January are estimated at 545,000 tonnes against PORLA's 637,899 tonnes in December.
There was little keen participation with many players mostly sidelined and some dealers expect the market to open mixed after the long holidays.
Dealing was thin with volume on the futures market totalling 731 lots at the close.
Gains in the futures market were marginal and dealers attributed the steadiness to underlying firm fundamentals.
Third month April futures saw some support at around 1,300 ringgit level and the contract closed three ringgit higher at 1,308 ringgit ($525.09) a tonne.

Physicals Feb (south) crude palm oil was offered 1,355 ringgit against bids of 1,347.50 after trading from 1,350 to 1,347.50. Feb (central) was offered at 1,355 and bids at 1,350 with early trades at 1,355 and Feb (north) at 1,350 against 1,342.50.
Mar (south) saw offers at 1,345 with bids at 1,340, with early trades reported at 1,345. Mar (central) saw offers at 1,340 against bids 1,332.50.
Among refined products, Feb RBD palm oil was offered at $570 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Mar at $565 and Apr/May/Jun at $557.50. Feb was traded at $567.50.
Feb RBD palm olein saw offers at $592.50, Mar at $595 and Apr/May/Jun at $587.50. Feb was traded $597.50, Mar at $592.50.
Feb/Mar RBD palm stearin was offered at $470 and Feb/Mar palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $307.50. -- Tan Lee Lee - (603-230-7510) ($1 =2.4910 ringgit)
